after: All of these (conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent) are separate factors to consider. People have their minds influenced without the conscious agreement of their adult self.

And all of this has got to lead somewhere, to a point where you notice you’re behaving more kindly, you’ve got more humility and better judgment than you had, you’re doing real service, or your ordinary life has gotten more workable.

For that starting point, I’ve taken familiar practices like modeling and supported action and built them into a kind of provisional bridge I call “borrowed adulthood,” but I’m not suggesting anyone has formally tested and proven the whole sequence as one treatment.

Keep it simple. Go into the trance to do one thing, starting from a single anchor or image and having one way of coming back, and set yourself a tone too if you want one (warm, bounded, directed, neutral witnessing, whatever). If you're going to use metaphors just do one, and if you switch metaphors, do it in a way that's conscious.

Using metaphors and imagery is entirely optional. You can use whatever form of signal shows up (feelings, rhythms, movements, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, lack of signal, whatever) but if you're using words, try to keep them related to whatever world you're creating. If you're going to count, do it in a way that makes sense in your world. And when you're done, come back the other way. (You can borrow qualities like warmth or steadiness as long as you don't change who you are.)

If you’re using fractionation, you come back up toward ordinary awareness and then decide whether to go into absorption again, and if you do it openly it teaches you that a trance has a way out as well as a way in. At some point in time you can add this, but you must say you are doing it before doing it, so no answer can secretly mean “deeper.”

To write an embedded invitation you take a small direction, one that invites a modest inner movement and doesn't hide a demand, and put it inside a larger sentence. ie. "And I can allow myself to experience..."

Reframes are dishonest when they make the problem into something that was good all along. Instead I’d have you ask yourself What else might be true? or What is this part trying to do for me? or How might my Nurturer reframe this? or How might my Protector reframe this? or How might my Guide reframe this? etc., etc.

Here is some inner child love. Put your hand over your heart and your other hand on your solar plexus, and say to yourself in a loving way, “Little one, you are not alone. You don’t have to fix it, I’m here now, and the adult is here now to listen to you,” and make sure you’re actually talking to your inner child, who is scared to death. If there’s no warmth today, just rest your hands there without faking anything and notice what you find.

For the no trance inner contact, I would do: Pacing: notice you can see, it's (day of the week), you have feet, you can read, you can write, etc. Suggestion: in your mind, ask one clear question and wait, but don't focus too hard. Choice: you can answer the question, write an answer, write that you don't know, take a break, rephrase the question, ask someone else, stop doing this, etc. Autonomous signal: you write down whatever you get (a word, sensation, impulse, objection, or silence), and you don't treat it as proof. Deepener: none here, though being fully alert isn't a lesser version. Handoff: have your adult self answer the question in whatever way is appropriate, and I'd rather that answer come through writing or doing something. Integration/exit: once you've reality tested the signal, do one small thing based on it. You just close the exercise there and carry on with your day, since you didn't go into trance.
